newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Malaysia's Petco to issue Kekway sell tender.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Petco to issue Kekway sell tender.

text.p: Malaysia's oil trading company Petco plans to issue a tender on Tuesday to sell the first shipment of Bunga Kekwah crude, an industry source said on Monday.
The tender will seek bids for 250,000 barrels of the crude for second-half August loading, the source said.
The source said the tender would close at 1430 hours (0630 GMT) on July 10 with validity to 1830 hours on the same day.

The new crude has an American Petroleum Institute (API) gravity of 36.5 degrees and a sulphur content of just 0.05 percent. The crude is expected to yield 40 percent gas oil and 40 percent low sulphur waxy residue.
It is expected to compete with Indonesia's Minas crude.
Kekwah production start up is expected at around 20,000 barrels per day (bpd) this month, building to 40,000 bpd by 2000.
Petco, a trading arm of state-owned oil giant Petronas, is to market the crude oil.

The consortium developing the field is made up of Petronas Carigali, with 46.06 percent, PetroVietnam Exploration and Production with 12.5 percent, Canada's International Petroleum Corp with 26.44 percent and Sands Petroleum AB SAPEfb.S with 15 percent.
